explicit_cast.quote: It prints 3.5; The (double) cast turns the division into a decimal division; so 7 / 2 gives 3.5 and that is stored in avg
explicit_cast.rule: wrong rule: (double) (3 / 5) is 0.6. Right rule: The integer division 3 / 5 = 0 happens inside the parentheses before the cast, so the result is 0.0; write (double) 3 / 5 to get 0.6.

expression.quote: The (double) cast turns the division into a decimal division; so 7 / 2 gives 3.5 and that is stored in avg
expression.rule: wrong rule: The type of a numerical expression depends on the type expected by the surrounding context, so double d = a / b; keeps the fraction. Right rule: The type of a numerical expression is determined by the expression, so double d = a / b; with int a and b still divides as ints.

integer_division.quote: The (double) cast turns the division into a decimal division; so 7 / 2 gives 3.5 and that is stored in avg
integer_division.rule: wrong rule: (double) (3 / 5) is 0.6. Right rule: The integer division 3 / 5 = 0 happens before the cast, so the result is 0.0.

type_conversion.quote: The (double) cast turns the division into a decimal division; so 7 / 2 gives 3.5 and that is stored in avg
type_conversion.rule: wrong rule: The type of a numerical expression depends on the type expected by the surrounding context, so double d = a / b; keeps the fraction. Right rule: The type of a numerical expression is determined by its operands, so double d = a / b; with int a and b still divides as ints and only then widens the result (1 / 3 gives 0.0).

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: The (double) cast turns the division into a decimal division; so 7 / 2 gives 3.5 and that is stored in avg
paths.logic: Points to LT (each / looks at its own two operand types when it is evaluated). Applied unevenly, a student evaluates 9/5 as 1.8 in f = (9/5)*c + 32 but as 1 elsewhere, or assumes a later double operand rescues an earlier int division. (here mixing in: "The type of a numerical expression depends on the type expected by the surrounding context, so double d = a / b; keeps the fraction")
